sections.heading: Core Gameplay Mechanics
sections.body:
At its core, Draw Rainbow Ninja is a game about drawing trajectories to eliminate enemies. The game takes place on a side-scrolling screen, with enemies appearing in waves. Players must use their mouse or finger to draw the perfect trajectory, taking into account the enemy's speed, distance, and any obstacles that may be in the way.

One of the key features of Draw Rainbow Ninja is its use of physics. The game's trajectories are governed by real-world physics, making it challenging to predict where the trajectory will land. This adds a layer of complexity to the game, making it more challenging and engaging for players.

The game also features a variety of power-ups and obstacles to keep players on their toes. Power-ups such as the 'ninja star' or 'rainbow sword' can help players take out multiple enemies at once, while obstacles like rocks or spikes can make it harder to reach the enemy.

As players progress through the game, the enemies get faster and more challenging to hit. This requires players to draw more precise trajectories and think strategically about their next move. The game also features a 'combo system', where players can earn bonus points for taking out multiple enemies in a row.
